title: feat(layout,app-shell,i18n): the runtime sidebar menu is not user-reorderable; the Pinned section keeps the user's order (objectui#12059)
body:
Fixes #12059
Clause-②: yes

The runtime sidebar no longer offers drag-to-reorder on the app's menu; the Pinned section is the one place a user orders entries. This **reverses objectui#11626**, which had extended menu drag-to-reorder to grouped sidebars; that card's pins move here (its two test files are deleted and replaced, its pending changeset is corrected, see below).

Maintainer's ruling (card body, verbatim): 「右侧浏览器，左侧菜单在用户界面不应该显示拖动按钮，拖动设计是studio的工作。」 Scope addition `6081436048`: 「补到 12059 上，按置顶区来做」, 「暂时不考虑编辑模式」.

## What changed

**Runtime sidebar (`UnifiedSidebar`, app-shell).** No drag grip and no menu reorder on any viewport: it stops passing `enableReorder` / `onReorder`, and `useNavOrder` is removed, so the `objectui-nav-order-APP` key is neither read nor written. A key left from before changes nothing (pinned below). Clearing it was allowed, not required; it is not cleared. The menu renders in the app's authored order.

**Pinned section (the scope addition).**
- A pinned row is dragged by the row itself. No grip at rest; the row's link gets `cursor: grab`, and a 2px insertion line marks where the row will land while dragging.
- Keyboard: with the pinned row's link focused, dnd-kit's `KeyboardSensor` with `sortableKeyboardCoordinates`: Space picks up, arrows move, Space drops, Escape cancels. Enter is deliberately NOT a start key (dnd-kit binds it by default): it still follows the link. No extra buttons, no extra focus stop: the link stays a link (dnd-kit's `role="button"` / `tabIndex` are not applied) and carries `aria-describedby` to dnd-kit's instructions; the live region announces pick-up, move and drop.
- A pointer drag carries the row under the pointer. A keyboard drag leaves it in place, dimmed, so it never covers the row it is over (measured in Chromium, below).
- The click a pointer drag ends with is swallowed. Measured in Chromium: without the guard, a drag released over the row's own external link navigated the page away (dnd-kit stops that click's propagation, so the router's `Link` never sees it, but nothing prevents its default).
- Persistence: the order is the order of the `type: 'nav'` favorites in the `UserDataAdapter`-backed favorites list (`nav:NAVID`), so it syncs exactly as the pins do. **No server-side change**: `createObjectStackUserStateAdapter` stores the whole list as one JSON `value` in `sys_user_preference` and hands it back as stored.
- Order rules: a new pin joins the end (a content favorite still goes first, as before); an unpin removes the entry and leaves the others in order; a re-pin joins the end again. A reorder fills the slots the named pins already hold, so a pin another app's sidebar draws, and every content favorite, keep their places. At the 20 nav-pin cap a new pin still joins the end and the earliest-pinned one rolls off (the documented "older entries roll off within their own bucket" keeps holding).
- No edit mode, no hide/show, no reset.

## Published surface (Clause-②: yes)

- `@object-ui/layout` — `NavigationRendererProps`: **removed** `enableReorder`, `onReorder`; **added** `pinnedOrder?: string[]`, `onPinnedReorder?: (pinnedIds: string[]) => void`. `AppSchemaRendererProps`: **removed** `enableReorder`, `onReorder` (a pass-through only; no in-repo caller passes them, only its own test did). Retired under the zero-pull rule; `RETIRED` comments mark both places.
- `@object-ui/app-shell` — `useFavorites()` return **gains** `reorderNavPins(navIds)`; `useNavPins()` return **gains** `reorderPins(orderedIds)`, and its `pinnedIds` is in the user's order. ⚠️ These two return members are surface the claim's file surface implied (the order "persists with the pins" in `useNavPins.ts` / the favorites store) but did not enumerate, and `FavoritesProvider.tsx` is a file beyond the claim's list; both are named in the report for the seat to amend the claim.
- `@object-ui/i18n` — `console.nav.dragToReorder` (the menu grip's label, zh 「拖动以重新排序」) **removed** from all ten packs: its only reader was the retired grip. `view.dragToReorder` is a different key and stays.
- Changeset `.changeset/12059-sidebar-no-reorder.md`: `minor` for layout, app-shell and i18n, with the breaking notes.

## Mechanism readings (dispatch zone 2)

1. **Favorites store order** — the store is a `FavoriteItem[]`; `pinnedNavIds` is built by walking it, so its iteration order is the array order. The write is `commit` → `saveFavorites` (localStorage) + the debounced `adapter.save(items)`, which the ObjectStack adapter upserts as the whole list in one `value`. No new field on the server record.
2. **Where the Pinned section renders** — inside `NavigationRenderer` itself (its `favoritesSection`, labelled `console.nav.favorites`), from `collectPinnedItems` over the tree. No separate component; it now goes through the new `PinnedNavigationList` when `onPinnedReorder` is passed.
3. **Callers of `enableReorder` / `onReorder`** — `UnifiedSidebar` (app arm) and `AppSchemaRenderer` (pass-through). **Studio's navigation editor does reorder, and not through `NavigationRenderer`:** `AppNavCanvas` (the Studio app designer's nav canvas) reorders the root list with native HTML5 drag-and-drop (`draggable` + `onDrop`); `plugin-designer` also has `NavigationDesigner` (a drag-and-drop tree builder) and `AppCreationWizard` (up/down buttons). No Studio edit.
4. **`objectui-nav-order-*`** — read and written only by `UnifiedSidebar`'s `useNavOrder`, now removed. The one other tracked spelling is the auth test `sessionUserChangePurge-5664.test.tsx`, which uses `objectui-nav-order-crm` as a stand-in for an un-namespaced key in a generic purge; it reads nothing from the sidebar and is untouched.
5. **「拖动以重新排序」** — `console.nav.dragToReorder`; pinned rows do not reuse it (no grip, the link keeps its own name), so it became dead and left all ten packs.

**Mobile:** `UnifiedSidebar` passes `enablePinning={!isMobile}` (unchanged, pin/unpin is out of scope), so a phone draws no Pinned section at all and there is nothing to reorder there; no touch sensor was added.

## Tests

- `packages/layout/src/__tests__/NavigationRenderer.pinnedOrder-12059.test.tsx` (new, 11): no menu row carries a grip, `aria-roledescription="sortable"`, the drag instructions or the grab cursor (grouped and group-free); the four retired props are pinned absent by `@ts-expect-error`; `pinnedOrder` orders the section (control: none ⇒ menu order); a pinned row is its own handle (one link + its pin button, no grip; control: no `onPinnedReorder` ⇒ plain row); keyboard reorder down and up through the real `KeyboardSensor` with the insertion line on the right edge of the right row and the dragged row held in place; Escape cancels and Enter never picks up (lit control: Space does); a pointer drag released over its own link does not let the browser follow it (control: a plain click does reach the window unprevented).
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/UnifiedSidebar.pinnedOrder-12059.test.tsx` (new, 4; real `NavigationRenderer`, real `useNavPins` over the real `FavoritesProvider`, an adapter standing in for the server row): no grip in the real sidebar; a stored `objectui-nav-order-crm` value (every level reversed) changes nothing; a keyboard reorder is saved through `adapter.save` with the unnamed pin and the starred record in place, and a fresh mount with nothing local draws it back from the adapter; a new pin goes to the end, an unpin leaves the order, a re-pin goes to the end.
- `packages/app-shell/src/context/__tests__/FavoritesProvider.navPinOrder-12059.test.tsx` (new, 4): append vs prepend, the slot-filling reorder and its persistence, an unknown id and a no-op order, the cap.
- Moved/retired: `NavigationRenderer.groupedReorder-11626.test.tsx` and `UnifiedSidebar.groupedNavOrder-11626.test.tsx` deleted (they pinned the reversed behaviour); `NavigationRenderer.listNesting-11690.test.tsx` keeps its axe pin over the new sortable pinned list instead of the menu reorder; the `AppSchemaRenderer.test.tsx` reorder case is removed; a stale bullet in `AppSchemaRenderer.mobileTabOrder-11395.test.tsx`'s header is updated.

## Reverse verification (predictions written before each run; every restore proven by blob hash = HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

| run | mutation | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV1 | the four source files back to `2a48bd40` | UnifiedSidebar test 4/4 red | 4 failed (grip found; stored order applied; keyboard did nothing; pins in tree order) |
| RV2 | `NavigationRenderer.tsx` back to `2a48bd40` | layout test 6 red / 5 green | 6 failed / 5 passed, the predicted six |
| RV2b | `NavigationRenderer.tsx` + `AppSchemaRenderer.tsx` back to base, layout `type-check` | TS2578 on the four retired-prop lines | TS2578 x4 on exactly those lines (plus the expected unknown-prop errors) |
| RV3 | drop the after-drag click guard | 1 red (pointer-drag click) | 1 failed / 10 passed; first attempt refused by `ablation-replace` (replacement text was a substring of the anchor, so its count could not rise; nothing ran), redone with a distinct marker |
| RV3b | same, in Chromium | the drag-to-self on the external link navigates away | navigated to the external URL; restored: stays put, plain click navigates (control) |
| RV4 | dnd-kit default keyboard codes | 1 red (Enter) | 1 failed / 10 passed |
| RV5 | no insertion line | 2 red (keyboard down / up) | 2 failed / 9 passed |
| RV6 | nav pin prepended again | 3 red across two files | 3 failed / 5 passed |
| RV8 | cap evicts the first in order | 1 red (cap) | 1 failed / 3 passed |
| RV9 | keyboard drag not held in place | 1 red (keyboard down) | 1 failed / 10 passed |

All test imports resolve `@object-ui/layout` through the vitest alias to `src`, so no `dist` rebuild sits between a mutation and its run.

## Browser (Chromium via Playwright, a temporary dev-only console page, never committed; server stopped by PID)

At rest: 0 grips, 0 `aria-roledescription`, 0 insertion lines; pinned link `cursor: grab`, menu link `cursor: pointer` with no `aria-describedby`. Keyboard: Space / ArrowDown drew one 2px line after the next row, the live region read the move, Space dropped, focus stayed on the moved link. Pointer: dragging the last pinned row to the top reordered it, no navigation, no reload. A drag released on its own internal link: no navigation; on its own external link: the page stayed (control: a plain click on that link navigated). No page errors.

The full app-shell suite is CI's.

- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the diff: NOT GOVERNED.

## Docs

`content/docs/guide/user-state-persistence.md` (reference rows, the pinned-order rules, an "Ordering the sidebar" paragraph) and `packages/app-shell/README.md` (user-scoped state). No guide page described dragging menu entries.

## Acceptance notes

- **The objectui#11626 changeset is still pending in the same release window.** Its body would have published that grouped-menu drag-to-reorder works and that the reorder props keep their types. Its prose is corrected (front matter untouched) to say it was retired before release; `check-changeset-overwrite` reports that modification, as designed.
- **Existing pins change order once.** Pins made before this change were prepended, so their stored order is newest first; they now draw in that order instead of menu order, until the user drags them. Stated in the changeset.
- **Announcements are dnd-kit's defaults** (English, entry ids), as the retired menu sort's were. Localizing them needs new pack keys, which the claim does not allow.
- **No `aria-roledescription` on pinned links**, on purpose: it would replace "link" in what a screen reader announces. The rows are described by dnd-kit's instructions instead.
- Pre-existing doc drift, not touched: the user-state guide's "Cross-device sync" line says a pin shows up on mobile, but the sidebar draws no Pinned section on mobile; its `useFavorites()` reference row also omits `refreshLabel`.
- Downstream (triage `6082337150`): objectstack-ai/objectstack#22487 must land no later than the objectstack console pin bump that carries this merge; the seat names the merge commit there after landing.
